paper_title: Stronger limits on hypothetical Yukawa interactions in the 40--8000 nm range
coupling_convention: |alpha|, dimensionless strength of Yukawa-type correction to Newtonian gravity (relative to gravity), exactly as plotted on the y-axis of Fig. 4
notes: Decca et al. 'Casimir-less' isoelectronic differential force measurement (IUPUI, arXiv:1410.7267) setting 95% CL limits on Yukawa corrections to Newtonian gravity, V = -(Gm1m2/r) alpha e^{-r/lambda}, over lambda = 30-8000 nm (Fig. 4). This is a fifth-force / Yukawa nucleon-coupled scalar constraint (ScalarNucleon). No numerical table is provided; the exclusion curve exists only as Fig. 4 (log-log, alpha from 1e-1 to 1e19). The emitted data points are order-of-magnitude reconstructions of the limit curve computed from the paper's Eq. (2) with the stated geometry (R=149.3 um, film thicknesses, densities) and the reported force sensitivity (~0.1-0.2 fN at tau=3000 s), consistent with the stated factor-1e3 improvement at lambda=300 nm. Mass conversion uses the paper's relation lambda = hbar/(m c), i.e. m[eV] = 197.33/lambda[nm]. Values are approximate (factor ~few uncertainty); alpha is relative-to-gravity strength, not a dimensionless g^2 coupling - downstream conversion to particle couplings requires alpha -> g via G m_n^2.
